UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                       
1                                                                        
                           DISTRICT OF NEVADA                            
2                                                                        
                                  * * *                                  
3                                                                        
    Michael Cirkunovs,                 Case No. 2:25-cv-00914-RFB-BNW    
4                                                                        
                   Plaintiff,                                            
5                                      ORDER                             
              v.                                                         
6                                                                        
    Zuffa LLC, et al.,                                                   
7                                                                        
                   Defendants.                                           
8                                                                        
9                                                                        
        Before this Court is Defendants’ motion seeking to seal and/or redact the brief and 
10                                                                        
   exhibits attached to its Statement of Missing Information (at ECF No. 72).1 ECF No. 79. No 
11                                                                        
   opposition has been filed.                                            
12                                                                        
   I.   Analysis                                                         
13                                                                        
        Generally, the public has a right to inspect and copy judicial records. Kamakana v. City &
14                                                                        
   Cnty. of Honolulu, 447 F.3d 1172, 1178 (9th Cir. 2006). Such records are presumptively publicly 
15                                                                        
   accessible. Id. Consequently, a party seeking to seal a judicial record bears the burden of 
16                                                                        
   overcoming this strong presumption. Id. In the case of dispositive motions, the party seeking to 
17                                                                        
   seal the record must articulate compelling reasons supported by specific factual findings that 
18                                                                        
   outweigh the general history of access and the public policies favoring disclosure, such as the 
19                                                                        
   public interest in understanding the judicial process. Id. at 1178-79 (alteration and internal 
20                                                                        
   quotation marks and citations omitted). The Ninth Circuit has further held that the full 
21                                                                        
   presumption of public access applies to technically non-dispositive motions and attached 
22                                                                        
   documents as well if the motion is “more than tangentially related to the merits of the case.” Ctr. 
23                                                                        
   for Auto Safety v. Chrysler Grp., LLC, 809 F.3d 1092, 1101 (9th Cir. 2016).  
24                                                                        
        Among the compelling reasons which may justify sealing a record are when such court 
25                                                                        
   files might have become a vehicle for improper purposes, such as the use of records to gratify 
26                                                                        
27                                                                        
1  private spite, promote public scandal, circulate libelous statements, or release trade secrets. 
2  Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1179 (quotation omitted). However, avoiding a litigant’s embarrassment, 
3  incrimination, or exposure to further litigation will not, without more, compel the court to seal its 
4  records. Id.                                                          
5       “[A] different standard applies to ‘private materials unearthed during discovery,’ as such 
6  documents are not part of the judicial record.” Pintos v. Pac. Creditors Ass'n, 605 F.3d 665 (9th 
7  Cir. 2010) (citing Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1180). Under Rule 26(c), a court may enter a protective 
8  order “to protect a party or person from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, or undue burden 
9  or expense.” “The relevant standard for purposes of Rule 26(c) is whether good cause exists to 
10  protect the information from being disclosed to the public by balancing the needs for discovery 
11  against the need for confidentiality.” Pintos, 605 F.3d at 678 (quotation omitted). Given the 
12  “weaker public interest in nondispositive materials,” the court applies the good cause standard in 
13  evaluating whether to seal documents attached to a nondispositive motion. Id. “Nondispositive 
14  motions ‘are often unrelated, or only tangentially related, to the underlying cause of action,’ and, 
15  as a result, the public’s interest in accessing dispositive materials does ‘not apply with equal 
16  force’ to non-dispositive materials.” Id. (citing Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1179). It is within the 
17  court’s discretion whether to seal documents. Id. at 679.             
18       Defendants seek to seal/redact several documents filed in a statement regarding missing 
19  documents. Because these documents are attached to a matter that is not dispositive or more than 
20  tangentially related to the merits of the case, this Court applies the good cause standard. 
21  Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1179.                                           
22       Good cause exists to seal/redact the exhibits in question.       
23       Exhibits 2-3, 5, 13, 35, and 43 contain detailed device and application inventories for 
24  Defendants’ employees and sensitive security information. The disclosure of this information 
25  risks exploitation and circumvention of security protocols, and therefore it should be sealed, as 
26  this Court has previously recognized. See Evans v. Nye Cnty., No. 2:20-cv-01919-RFB-VCF, 
27  2023 WL 362818, at *13 (D. Nev. Jan. 19, 2023) (Boulware, J.) (sealing sensitive security 
1       Exhibit 4 is an instant or text message thread. The redacted portions contain personally 
2  identifying information (“PII”) (phone numbers) and nonpublic strategy, negotiation, or 
3  operational content. Redaction of PII is authorized by rule and local practice. Fed. R. Civ. P. 5.2; 
4  LR IC 6-1. Where the messages discuss competitively sensitive business information, good cause 
5  exits to apply Defendant’s proposed redactions on that basis as well. First 100 LLC v. Omni Fin., 
6  LLC, No. 2:16-cv-00099-RFB-CWH, 2016 WL 5661916, at *1 (D. Nev. Sept. 29, 2016) 
7  (Boulware, J.) (“Protecting proprietary information from public knowledge is sufficient under the 
8  stricter ‘compelling reasons’ standard, and is therefore sufficient in this instance in which the 
9  lower ‘good cause’ standard applies.”). Courts routinely seal confidential business information, 
10  internal financials, and sensitive security materials from competitive misuse or operational 
11  compromise.                                                           
12       Exhibit 1 is an internal organizational chart. Courts in this District have sealed 
13  organizational charts because they contain “confidential internal business deliberations, 
14  organization, and capabilities.” Clark v. Metropolitan Life Ins. Co., No. 3:08-cv-00158-LRH-
15  VPC, 2010 WL 1006823, at *1 (D. Nev. Mar. 16, 2010).                  
16       Exhibits 11, 14, 26, and 40 contain nonpublic payments, contractual obligations, and 
17  negotiation positions, which would cause competitive harm and prejudice future negotiations if 
18  disclosed, particularly where the privacy interests of unrelated counterparties is threatened. See 
19  Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1179–80.                                        
20       Exhibits 7, 9, and 10 relate to agreements are not related to the underlying litigation, and 
21  therefore any corresponding benefit to public access is low. Additionally, unsealing these 
22  agreements will harm Defendants’ relationships with the non-parties who are counterparties to the 
23  agreements, given that it was the parties’ express understanding that the agreements would be 
24  kept confidential. Leftenant v. Blackmon, No. 2:18-CV-01948-EJY, 2020 WL 6747710, at *3 (D. 
25  Nev. Nov. 17, 2020).                                                  
26       Exhibits 8, 18-20, 32, and 38-39 are email chains and agreements containing PII. As 
27  mentioned above, redaction of PII is allowed by the local rules. Additionally, disclosure of non-
1 || Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 1179-80; In re Elec. Arts, Inc., 298 F. App'x 568, 569-570 (9th Cir. 2008) 
2 || (explaining that competitive harm exists where information is given to “competitors who do not 
3 || know or use it” and “might harm a  litigant’s competitive standing.”). 
4          Lastly, the brief at ECF No. 72 references the contents of the exhibits discussed above or 
5 || similar documents. 
6 ||  I.     CONCLUSION 
7          IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED that Defendants’ Motion to Seal at ECF No. 79 is 
8 || GRANTED. 
9          IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Clerk of Court is directed to maintain under seal 
10 |)  the exhibits at ECF No. 74. 
11          IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Clerk of Court is directed to unseal ECF No. 72 
12 ||  as that filling does not contain any of the information the Defendants seek to maintain under seal. 
13 
14 
15 
16          DATED: December 17, 2025 
17 

19                                              B     DA   WEKSLER 
50                                              UNITED STATES MAGISTRATE JUDGE
